settings.description: The most characters a chat's title may have.
The most results one search over chats returns.
About how many words of a matching message a search result shows, from 1 to 64.
The registry name of the model a new chat uses. Empty means the first usable model in the person's registry.
The most turns that may wait in one chat behind the one that is running.
The most model calls one turn may make, counting each call that follows a tool.
The most tokens a chat reply may hold. Zero means the model's own limit.
The most tokens a model may spend on thinking in a chat turn. Zero asks for no thinking.
How often an open turn stream looks for new events when nothing has woken it.
The most stored events a turn stream reads from the database at a time.
How long the stop route waits for a turn to end before it answers.
Whether a chat is given a title after its first reply.
The registry name of the model that writes chat titles. Empty means the model that answered the chat.

settings.default: Write a title of at most six words for the chat that begins below. Answer with the title alone, with no quotation marks and no full stop.
settings.description: The instruction given to the model that writes a chat's title.
The most tokens the model may write for a chat's title.
How many characters of the first message, and of the first reply, the title model is shown.
How long the title model may take before the title is made from the first message.
How many words of the first message make a title when no model writes one.
The context window, in tokens, the test tenant's recorded turns are checked against.
The output limit, in tokens, of the test tenant's recorded turns.

settings.default: You are the assistant in Keystone, a private workspace for one person. Answer plainly, and say so when you do not know something.
settings.description: The standing instructions every chat call starts with. Empty sends none.
The share of a model's input room a chat call may fill, from 1 to 100. The room is the context window less what is kept for the reply.
The most earlier turns of a chat one call carries. Zero means as many as fit.
The most attachments and attached chats may take of a call, as a percentage of the room left after the rules, the tools and the current message.
The most recalled knowledge may take of a call, as a percentage of the room left after the rules, the tools and the current message. That much is held for it ahead of earlier turns.
The most the summary of older history may take of a call, as a percentage of the room left after the rules, the tools and the current message. That much is held for it ahead of earlier turns.

settings.default: The earliest part of this chat is not shown to you, because the whole chat no longer fits. If the person refers to something you cannot see, say so and ask.
settings.description: What the model is told when earlier turns of a chat were left out of a call. Empty tells it nothing.
How many times a call is packed again, smaller, when the provider counts more tokens in it than Keystone estimated.
Whether the oldest turns of a long chat are summarised, and the summary sent in their place. Off, they are left out with a note, as before.

When the earlier turns of a chat that are not yet summarised take more than this share of the room a call has for them, from 1 to 100, the oldest are summarised. A turn that is left out is summarised whatever the share.

The oldest turns are summarised until the rest take no more than this share of the room, from 0 to less than chats.compact_trigger_percent. The gap between the two is how far a chat grows between one summary and the next.
The most tokens a chat's summary may take, as Keystone estimates them. Its share of a call, chats.context_summary_percent, may make it less.

settings.default: A summary of the earlier part of this chat. The turns it stands for are not shown to you.
settings.description: The line a call is given before the summary of a chat's oldest turns.

settings.default: You keep the running summary of a long chat in Keystone, a private workspace for one person. You are given the summary so far, if there is one, and the turns of the chat that follow it. Write one summary that takes them all in: what the person asked for and why, what was decided, the facts, names and numbers that matter, what they prefer, and what is still open. Keep what the summary so far says unless a later turn changes it. Write plain prose about the person and the assistant, in at most {words} words, and answer with the summary alone.
settings.description: The instruction given to the model that summarises a chat's oldest turns. {words} becomes the most words the summary may have.
The most characters of one message the summary model is shown.
The most model calls one summary of a chat may make, each taking in as many turns as the summary model's window holds.
How long one summary call may take before it is given up, and the oldest turns are left out with the note.
How long a chat whose summary failed waits before it is tried again.

settings.default: A message from earlier in this chat that the person pinned, so it is always shown to you.
settings.description: The line a call is given before a pinned message whose turn is not sent.
